_comment: FACTORtv — QUALIFYING and PRACTICE.
A session with no overtakes, no meaningful gaps and no story of
position. The drama is the timesheet: who is on top of it, who has
found time, and how long is left to find some.
RacerTV's observations, and they are the ones you only get from
watching: most of qualifying is an EMPTY track, and the states that
actually need a line are nobody-has-set-a-time, only-one-driver-has,
everyone-is-in-the-pits and there-is-only-one-car-here. A booth with
nothing to say about an empty session says the same three things about
a full one.
There is deliberately no 'lap deleted' category: this build does not
populate per-car lap validity, and inventing a deletion the timing
screen disagrees with would cost more trust than the line is worth.
`quali_pole` MUST NOT use {gap}. The first driver to set a time takes
provisional pole with no margin over anybody, so the slot is empty and
the line airs as 'Top of the sheets, and it's Derek Warwick by !' —
which is exactly what went out in the 2026-08-16 test run. Asserted in
tests/flowtest.py.
Extra slots: {set} drivers with a time, {total} in the session,
{p1} {p2} {p3} the provisional top three, {t} a lap time.
`quali_lap_praise` is Chuck reacting to a benchmark lap, and it is
gated by `_quali_lap_notable()`: an early pole means nothing,
because the man has beaten nobody and will be beaten shortly. It
fires when the session is into its closing stretch, or most of the
field has run, or the lap took a big chunk out of the old best.
TOP AND TAIL. `quali_top3` reads the same three names as
`quali_standings` but WITH the margins: {t} pole lap, {g2} P1 to P2,
{g3} P2 to P3. `quali_margin_big` / `quali_margin_slim` qualify a new
pole by how far clear it is, measured against the RUNNER-UP's lap and
not against the improvement on the old benchmark — a driver can take
half a second off himself and still lead by a hundredth.
`quali_duel` is two drivers trading the top spot ({a} and {b}, {n}
changes). It outranks a single fast lap because it is the story of the
session rather than an event in it.
`quali_tail` / `quali_offpace` / `quali_player_offpace` cover the
bottom of the sheet. They are gated on a real field, most of it having
run, and a measurable deficit — a driver who has not been out yet is
not slow, he is absent. The lines may say the pace is not in the car,
but only as Chuck's OPINION: we cannot see a setup sheet.
`quali_lap_sector` / `quali_lap_allround` say WHERE a benchmark lap
was won. Real data: rF2's mBestLapSector1/2 are the sectors OF THE
BEST LAP, so the three add up to that lap and comparing them against
the benchmark they beat is honest. A 'theoretical best' assembled
from three different laps would not be — that lap was never driven.
Slots: {sec} the sector, {gap} the time found there, {drv}.
